v7.interpretation: No gain in complete replies. Fewer identifiable critical claims while most replies are incoherent does not constitute improved factual competence.

c7.interpretation: No gain in complete replies. Fewer identifiable critical claims while most replies are incoherent does not constitute improved factual competence.

prospectiveInterpretationForNextExperime: Use the same frozen 40-turn development suite, same engine and generation settings, and actual prior assistant replies.

A real fact/current-request gain requires a new complete reply that answers this turn, preserves user facts/corrections and remains understandable Spanish, not just copies a name or an irrelevant correct fact.
Inspect matched-turn gains and losses together; an entity recovered on one turn cannot compensate for new factual errors on its following corrected turns.
Count full four-turn dialogs. Correct isolated first turns with breakdown under own generated history do not establish conversation coherence.
Grade partials only for substantive correct requested content. Mere token/name echo, generic support in place of a requested fact, or incomprehensible fragments remain failed.
Critical counts cover identifiable frozen forbidden assertions only; silence, refusal, repetition and incoherence can lower critical counts while leaving factual competence unchanged.
Report technical budget stops and context truncation alongside semantic outcomes. Fewer completed claims caused by technical failure must not appear as safety improvement.
Lower validation NLL is training evidence, not improvement in free conversation. No reserved cases or results may guide experiment choice.
The final acceptance requires 36/40 complete replies, 8/10 complete dialogs and zero critical/technical failures; development comparison does not constitute reserved acceptance.
